hypothesis: The only training failure was a single case, so the evidence for this is thin. In that case (mqx-071) the doctor found the deciding sign itself: bilateral decreased hearing on the cranial nerve exam. It then threw the finding away because the patient said his hearing hadn't changed, and noted it only as an unresolved gap. It also never ordered audiometry, which was in the case file. On top of that it kept re-requesting HINTS exam parts the record said weren't there, and settled on the more common neighbouring diagnosis (vestibular neuritis) instead of the one that explains every finding (labyrinthitis). The general failure is submitting a diagnosis that leaves an abnormal objective finding unexplained, especially when the patient's lay report contradicts it, and when the alternative is a close variant that differs by exactly that feature. This likely also accounts for some dev-set misses I can't see (baseline dev accuracy 0.775), since many USMLE pairs are separated by a single finding. The fix is a pre-submission check: every abnormal finding must be accounted for, objective findings beat the patient's report, pick between near-twin diagnoses on the separating feature, and name the specific disease.
changes: harness/lessons.md (was empty): added short general lessons. (1) The final diagnosis must explain every abnormal finding; settle discrepancies with an objective test rather than listing them as gaps. (2) Exam and test findings beat the patient's lay self-report. (3) Pick between closely related diagnosis pairs using the one feature that separates them, and look for that feature on purpose. (4) Stop re-requesting exams or tests the record doesn't have, and order the simple test aimed at the organ involved early. (5) Name the specific disease, not a category, and put only one condition in the diagnosis field.
harness/system.md: added a three-point check to run before submit_diagnosis (do all abnormal findings fit, is there a near-twin diagnosis, is the name specific enough). config.json is unchanged.
expected_effect: The doctor should stop submitting the common neighbour diagnosis when the case contains a finding that points to the more specific variant, for example labyrinthitis over vestibular neuritis, or nephritic over nephrotic syndrome. It should also stop spending requests on exam parts the record doesn't have. I expect a small gain in held-out accuracy at roughly the same question and request counts, with little risk to the cases it already gets right, because the change only adds a reconciliation step before submitting.
